Review a code change with the `mattpocock-skills:code-review` skill (load it via the Skill tool first and follow it). Repo: /home/wolf/speeddev-runner/checkouts/wolfsoko/wol-sok-mono/529, branch `3103-step-3-cloud-entry`, fixed point `origin/main` (review `git diff origin/main...HEAD`). It is PR #3139 of GitHub issue WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono#3103.

The spec is the section "# Step 3: the `/cloud` entry" at the end of `docs/specs/3103-arch-feat-shared-bacteria-engine-mixes-simulation-cloud-contract-and-3-2k-lines-of-ui-texts-behind-one-791-line-barrel.md` (the plan is the matching section in `docs/plans/` with the same file name). Standards are the root `CLAUDE.md` and `libs/features/bacteria-engine/CLAUDE.md`.

The change in short: names declared under `libs/features/bacteria-engine/src/lib/state/cloud/` leave the engine's main entry `src/index.ts` and move to a new entry `src/cloud.ts` (`@wolsok/feat-shared-bacteria-engine/cloud`). It is wired through `tsconfig.base.json`, `tools/federation/workspace-federation.js` and an ng-packagr secondary entry `libs/features/bacteria-engine/cloud/ng-package.json`. Consumers in `apps/bacteria-wars-functions`, `libs/features/lazy/bacteria-game` and `apps/bacteria-game-remote` split their imports. There are two specs: the new `src/entries.spec.ts` and the updated `src/engine-bundle.spec.ts`.

Things worth checking: does any consumer still import a cloud name from the main entry, or a non-cloud name from `/cloud`? Are the imports duplicated, or left as empty or awkward statements? Does `entries.spec.ts` really prove the spec's acceptance 1? Do the docs match the code? Does anything break the federation or ng-packagr build (types declared twice in dist, for example)? You may run `npx jest -c libs/features/bacteria-engine/jest.config.ts <file>` for single specs. Don't run the whole affected suite: the machine is heavily loaded.

Change no files. Report the findings in order of severity, each with file:line, what is wrong and a concrete fix. Say plainly if you find nothing that matters.

# CLAUDE.md — wol-sok-mono

Angular + Nx monorepo. Read this before touching anything.

## Stack

- **Angular 22** — standalone components, zoneless change detection, Signals, `@if`/`@for`/`@switch` control flow
- **Nx 23** — monorepo orchestration, caching, affected commands
- **TypeScript 6.0** — strict mode
- **Build**: Vite (Analog/Vitest apps), Webpack + Module Federation (angular-examples)
- **Testing**: Jest (most unit tests), Vitest (Vite projects), Playwright (E2E)
- **Lint / Format**: oxlint (`.oxlintrc.json`, targets inferred by `@nx/oxlint`), angular-eslint for templates only (`eslint.config.mjs`, target `lint-templates`) and oxfmt (`.oxfmtrc.json`, driven by `nx format`)
- **UI**: Angular Material + CDK everywhere (no custom primitives if AM covers it)
- **State**: Angular Signals (local/sync), RxJS (async), NgRx Signal Store (bacteria game), Akita/Elf (older app-wide stores)
- **Backend**: Firebase (Hosting, Auth, DB), AWS CDK (S3/CloudFront infra)
- **Package manager**: npm (use `npm ci`, never yarn/pnpm)

## Project Layout

```
apps/                   # Deployable apps
  angular-examples/     # Main showcase (Webpack + Module Federation)
  pacetrainer/          # Pace trainer (Vite + Analog.js)
  rollapolla-analog/    # Analog.js SSR demo
  *-remote/             # Module Federation remotes
  *-cdk/                # AWS CDK infra stacks
  bacteria-wars-android/ # Android app (Gradle, Trusted Web Activity)
libs/
  features/             # Domain features (can use shared + utils + ui-kit)
  shared/               # Cross-cutting concerns (can use utils)
  utils/                # Pure utilities (minimal deps)
  ui-kit/               # Reusable UI components
  public/               # Published npm packages (e.g. @wolsok/thanos)
  fib-wasm/             # WebAssembly modules
  test-helper/          # Testing utilities
tools/                  # Build/deploy node scripts
docs/                   # Architecture, testing, getting-started docs
```

## Essential Commands

```bash
# Install
npm ci

# Serve
npx nx serve pacetrainer
npx nx serve angular-examples

# Build
npx nx build <project> [--configuration production]

# Test
npx nx test <project>
npx nx run <project>:e2e

# Lint (always --fix)
npx nx lint <project> --fix            # oxlint
npx nx lint-templates <project> --fix  # angular-eslint template rules
npm run lint                          # all projects, both targets

# Format (REQUIRED before committing)
npx nx format:write

# Affected only (prefer in CI / large PRs)
npx nx affected -t build,test,lint,lint-templates

# Dependency graph
npx nx graph
```

## Engineering Principles (mandatory)

Long-term, strategic software engineering is required. A change that works but leaves the code harder to change is not done.

- **Improve the codebase with every feature and bug fix.** Leave the code you touch cleaner than you found it: extract duplication, split oversized files/functions/components, fix misleading names, remove dead code, and add missing tests around what you changed.
- **Fix root causes, not symptoms.** No workarounds or one-off special cases when the underlying design is the problem; fix the design.
- **Stay modular.** Small, focused units with one responsibility and narrow interfaces. Put logic in the right `libs/` layer (see Dependency Constraints) instead of growing app code; keep domain logic out of components and in testable services/stores/pure functions.
- **Clean Code is the standard.** Intention-revealing names, small functions, no magic values, no deep nesting, no copy-paste, single level of abstraction per function, explicit error handling.
- **Easy to maintain beats clever.** Prefer simple, readable code a newcomer can follow over terse or tricky solutions.
- **Scope of cleanup:** improvements to the code your change touches belong in the same PR. A larger refactor that the change exposes but doesn't need goes in its own PR (or an issue), so each PR stays reviewable.

## Coding Rules

1. **Standalone components only** — no NgModules
2. **Zoneless change detection** — never add `zone.js` imports or zone-dependent patterns
3. **Signals for state** — prefer `signal()`/`computed()`/`effect()` over manual subscriptions where possible
4. **OnPush everywhere** — `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`
5. **Angular Material** — use AM components consistently; don't roll custom UI that AM already covers
   - Exception (pacetrainer): the countdown ring (`pace-countdown-circle`) is a custom SVG, since `mat-progress-spinner` has no track ring
   - Exception (bacteria game): the stage's busy indicator (`feat-lazy-bac-game-bacteria-spinner`) is plain HTML and CSS, since it must keep moving on the compositor while the work it covers blocks the main thread
6. **Modern control flow** — `@if`, `@for`, `@switch` (not `*ngIf`, `*ngFor`, `*ngSwitch`)
7. **2-space indentation**, kebab-case filenames, `*.spec.ts` for tests
8. **Explicit `public`/`private`** in class members
9. **Strongly typed** — avoid `any`; use proper generics
10. **English in code** — identifiers, file and folder names, persisted field and storage key names, comments, commit messages, specs, plans and ADRs are English; texts the user sees stay in the app's UI language (German in Korbjäger and Pacetrainer). A domain term from `CONTEXT.md` takes its `_Code_` name (Kind is `Child`, Spiel `Game`, Kader `Roster`), never an ad-hoc translation. Fields of an outside API keep its spelling (the DBB's `ligaData`, `spielplan`) and get English names at the adapter. Korbjäger's existing German identifiers and Firestore fields are renamed by their own issues ([#2966](https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/issues/2966) the fields, then [#2967](https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/issues/2967) the identifiers), not piecemeal: persisted names need a migration. Pacetrainer's identifiers are English since [#2968](https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/issues/2968). Every non-persisted name a change introduces or rewrites is English
11. **Device storage through `@wolsok/utils-browser-storage`** — read, write and watch `localStorage` with `deviceStorage`, `readStored`/`writeStored`, `readStoredJson`/`writeStoredJson` and `watchStored` (`libs/utils/browser-storage`), never with a `try`/`catch` of your own: a missing, blocked or unreadable storage reads as nothing stored, a refused write keeps nothing and reports `'full'` or `'refused'`. Only `LocalAnswerCache` (`feat-korbjaeger-answers`), which evicts per failed write, keeps its own loop, and Korbjäger's `dropKeysBeforeEnglishNames` (`keys-before-english-names.ts`, transitional) keeps its guard until it goes

## Linting & Formatting

- One workspace-wide `.oxlintrc.json`; there are no per-project lint configs. Add project-specific rules through `overrides` with a `files` glob.
- Type-aware linting is on (`options.typeAware`, backed by `oxlint-tsgolint`). It reads each project's `tsconfig.json` with TypeScript 7 semantics: no `baseUrl`, `paths` relative to `tsconfig.base.json` (`./libs/...`), and no `moduleResolution: node`/`node10`. Keep new tsconfigs on that layout or lint reports `tsconfig-error`.
- `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries` runs inside oxlint through the `@nx/oxlint/boundaries-plugin` bridge; tag constraints live in `.oxlintrc.json`.
- Boundaries are never disabled inline: `wolsok/no-boundary-disable` (`tools/oxlint/workspace-rules.mjs`, the workspace's own JS plugin, a leaf project `oxlint-workspace-rules`: `@nx/oxlint` gives every project an implicit edge on a local plugin's project, so it must import nothing from the workspace) fails on `eslint-disable`/`oxlint-disable` comments for the rule. Move the import behind a lib's path alias, or record the exception as an override in `.oxlintrc.json` (as for `apps/*/federation.config.js` and `libs/utils/version`). That project's `namedInputs` `default` and `production` are empty, so the edge feeds no other project's `build`, `deploy` or `test` and a rule change releases nothing (#3015), while every `lint` still reads the plugin file; a target added to it names its inputs explicitly, as its `lint` and `test` do (`release-affected.test.mjs` checks every one).
- The workspace version (`version.json`) is read only through `@wolsok/utils-version` (`libs/utils/version`, `WORKSPACE_VERSION`, `releaseName(project)`), which declares the file as an input, so every task depending on it reruns on a release. `wolsok/no-version-json-read` (in the same `tools/oxlint/workspace-rules.mjs`) fails any other import or `read…()` of the file within one expression (`readFileSync(join(root, 'version.json'))`), but traces no path built in an earlier statement; `libs/utils/version` is exempt by an override in `.oxlintrc.json`. The plugin's spec runs the rules through oxlint itself: `npx nx test oxlint-workspace-rules`.
- Production sources never import test-only code: `wolsok/no-testing-import` (same plugin, on for `apps/*/src/**` and `libs/**/src/**` by an override in `.oxlintrc.json`) fails an import, `export … from`, `import()`, `import('…').Type`, `import x = require('…')` or `require()` of a `@wolsok/<lib>/testing` entry or a relative `testing` path, since those fakes call `jest.fn`/`vi.fn` at module load and the boundary rule counts `<lib>/testing` as `<lib>`. A lib that is test-only as a whole without a `testing` entry (`@wolsok/shared-firebase-emulator`) is named in `TEST_ONLY_LIBS` and counts with every entry; a new one goes there. Test files there are recognised by their path inside the workspace (`TEST_FILES`: `*.spec.*`, `*.test.*`, `*.emulator.*` outside an `environments/` folder, whose `environment.emulator.ts` is a build configuration, `*.cy.*`, `*.mock.*`, `test-setup.*`, a `testing.ts` entry, anything below `testing/`); `tools/` and `e2e/` are not linted by it.
- The scripts under `tools/` are the project `tools` (tag `tools`, never depending on an app), with an inferred `lint`, `typecheck-tools` (`tsc` of `tools/tsconfig.tools.json`, `.ts` only) and `test` (`node --test` of every `tools/**/*.test.mjs`). A module an app imports gets a nested project of its own (`tools/federation` is `tools-federation`, `tools/vite` is `tools-vite`): Nx records the app's import as a dependency, so inside `tools` every script's change would release the apps. Scripts import libs only through their path aliases, never a relative path into a lib's `src/` (the balance lab takes the engine's `/balance` entry, the fixture scripts the basketball data lib's `/testing`), and run as `tsx --tsconfig tools/tsconfig.tools.json`, since tsx reads only a root `tsconfig.json`, which the workspace lacks; `tools/tsconfig.json` only extends `tsconfig.tools.json`, so type-aware oxlint, which takes a file's nearest `tsconfig.json`, resolves those aliases too.
- oxlint only lints JS/TS. Angular templates are covered by a second, template-only ESLint setup: the root `eslint.config.mjs` (angular-eslint template rules for `.html` and inline templates, plus the per-project component/directive selector prefixes) is inferred as the `lint-templates` target by `@nx/eslint/plugin`. New Angular projects get their selector prefix added to `selectorPrefixes` in that file. The JSON-based `@nx/dependency-checks` rule is gone; keep package.json deps correct by hand.
- `nx format:write` / `nx format:check` run oxfmt (HTML, SCSS, Markdown and YAML are formatted through its Prettier-backed path).
- The SpeedDev cockpit (skill, roles, hooks) reaches sessions as the `speeddev` plugin on the claude.ai account, not as repo files; don't add `.claude/skills/cockpit/` or `.claude/hooks/cockpit/` back.

## Dependency Constraints

```
apps        → features, shared, utils, ui-kit
features    → shared, utils, ui-kit
shared      → utils
utils       → (minimal external deps only)
public      → (own deps only, published packages)
```

Do not create circular dependencies. Run `npx nx graph` to verify.

## Target Policy

- Root `.browserslistrc` and `tsconfig.base.json` govern everything — apps/libs inherit.
- **Do not bump targets in `libs/public/*`** — published packages, held back for consumer compat.
- **`apps/*-cdk` use `target: "ESNext"`** intentionally (Node runtime) — exclude from browser-target changes. Their `tsconfig.json` extends the root `tsconfig.cdk.json`, which holds that target; a new CDK app extends it too, never `tsconfig.base.json` directly.

## Native Federation

- `angular-examples` is the shell, remotes are `fourier-analysis-remote`, `bacteria-game-remote`, `shader-examples-remote`.
- Shared setup lives in `tools/federation/workspace-federation.js`; each app's `federation.config.js` only adds its name and `exposes`. A package skipped in one app must be skipped in all of them, or the shell and a remote disagree about the import map. The game lib's secondary entries (`admin-kit`, `watch`, and `testing`, the fake Firebase SDK the admin's specs take), its engine (`@wolsok/feat-shared-bacteria-engine`, with `/testing` and the balance lab's `/balance`), its rendering (`@wolsok/feat-bacteria-rendering`) and its sound (`@wolsok/feat-bacteria-sound`) are skipped there with the lib.
- `exposes` paths resolve from the workspace root (`./apps/<app>/src/...`), not the project root.
- **Nothing but the exposed module belongs in `src/app/remote-entry/`.** Native Federation maps the whole _directory_ of an exposed file to the remote's public name, so a sibling file imported with a static `import` from outside that folder is rewritten to `<remote>/Routes` and its exports vanish at runtime. That is why each remote's bootstrap component sits in `src/app/`, not next to `entry.routes.ts`.
- A remote also has to run standalone (its own e2e serves it that way), so check both: loaded through the shell _and_ opened on its own port.
- Remotes are listed in `apps/angular-examples/src/assets/federation.manifest.json` (dev) and `federation.manifest.prod.json` (prod).
- Every singleton a remote shares must be shared by the shell at the same version, or inside the shell the remote loads a second copy (for `firebase/*`, a second `@firebase/app` registry), since `ignoreUnusedDeps` prunes each app's shared entries to its own imports. `federation-shared-singletons:test` (`tools/federation/shared-singletons/`, #3085) compares the `remoteEntry.json` of the shell's build with each remote's of its prod manifest after the builds and fails on a gap; a new remote goes into that project's `implicitDependencies` too (its spec checks it, and that both manifests list the same remotes). Its tag is `tools` although it depends on apps: the edges are `implicitDependencies` on their build output, never an import.
- Each app has an `esbuild` target (`@angular/build:application`) wrapped by a `build`/`serve` target from `@angular-architects/native-federation`. Change build options on `esbuild`.
- `bacteria-game-remote` runs on Firebase Hosting (`firebase.bacteria-game-remote.json`, site `bacteria-wars`, domain `bacteria-wars.wolsok.de`), deployed by its `deploy` target together with the Firestore and Realtime Database rules. The shell's prod manifest loads the remote from there, and the shell reloads once when a navigation fails on a remote bundle a release replaced (`core/reload-on-stale-bundle.ts`). The old domain `bacteria-game.wolsok.de` is gone; `bacteria-game-remote-cdk` (stack `BacteriaGame`) only holds the new domain's CNAME, whose construct id must stay as it is.
- The game's legal pages live in `bacteria-game-remote`, not the lib: `/privacy` and `/impressum` (`src/app/privacy`, `src/app/impressum`, sharing `src/app/legal/`). Both name the provider from `SITE_OWNER` (`@wolsok/shared-legal`, `libs/shared/legal`: name, email, postal address, VAT ID), shown by its `SiteOwnerComponent` (`<wolsok-site-owner>`), as on RollaPolla's and wolsok.de's `/privacy` and `/impressum`, which also fills `siteOwner` in the support options for the footer's copyright line. The game lib's `support/` folder links to the pages from the footer under the main menu (the route paths are the lib's `legal-links.ts`, used by `app.routes.ts`) and offers the Android app or the PWA in a banner (`InstallOffer`), both only where `provideGameSupport` is set up: on the game's own site, never in the shell.
- The owner's admin area (ADR 0012) is the lib `feat-lazy-bacteria-wars-admin` (tag `feature:admin`, prefix `feat-lazy-bac-admin`), loaded by `/admin` in `bacteria-game-remote`'s `app.routes.ts` only, never through the exposed routes. It takes from the game only `@wolsok/feat-lazy-bac-game/admin-kit` (and, in its specs only, `@wolsok/feat-lazy-bac-game/testing`), has texts of its own in English and German, and must stay out of what every visitor loads: the remote's production `build` ends with `tools/bacteria-game/check-lazy-admin.mjs`, which fails when the admin's sources reach `main`, the polyfills or `Routes`.
- Exception: `bacteria-game-remote` is also a standalone PWA. Its federation build is `build-federation`; `build` then reruns `ngsw-config`, since the federation builder writes its files after Angular has hashed the output into `ngsw.json`.
- Error reports go to Sentry (org `wolsok`): the shell to `angular-examples` (`bootstrap.ts`, `core/core.module.ts`), the game to `bacteria-wars`, started only by the remote's standalone `bootstrap.ts` and `app.config.ts` (`src/app/error-reports/`), never by the lib or the exposed routes, and only where the environment has a `sentry` block (`environment.prod.ts`). The SDK is imported dynamically (`import()` in `error-reports.ts`), so it stays off the start's path; errors from before it loaded wait for it. Import it nowhere else but as a type. Errors only and no personal data (owner's decision of 2026-10-26): no tracing, Replay or sessions, `dataCollection.userInfo: false`, and `scrub.ts` drops the user, strips query, hash (`#friend=…`) and id-like tokens, and the attributes of click breadcrumbs (avatars name players in `aria-label` and `alt`). `@sentry/angular` is skipped in `workspace-federation.js`, so each app bundles its own copy. The release is `bacteria-wars@v<version.json>` (`releaseName('bacteria-wars')` from `@wolsok/utils-version`), created by `.github/actions/create-release`; a change to what is sent goes into the privacy policy (section 10) too.
- A `chunk-*` file that a federation build's `importmap.json` names under `@nf-internal/` (imported only by shared bundles, say the game's 47 kB chunk with `@firebase/app` and `@firebase/util`) is no duplicate: Native Federation builds all shared packages in one esbuild run with code splitting, and the code they have in common lands in those chunks. Where the shell shares the same packages (today it shares the same seven `firebase/*` entries as the game), only the shell's chunk loads; on its own site the remote's loads once. They count towards `allScript` like the bundles themselves, and the `@firebase/*` sub-packages need no `shared` or `skip` entry (#3063). A `chunk-*` holding an app's or a skipped lib's own code is a different case.
- Fonts and icons are self-hosted: each app's global `styles.scss` imports the Fontsource faces (latin subsets) and `material-icons/iconfont/filled.css`, and nothing loads from Google Fonts (Angular's font inlining fetched them at build time, which failed the release build, and Google would get every visitor's IP). The shell imports the game's faces too (Atkinson Hyperlegible, Bricolage Grotesque, Cookie), since only the remote's JavaScript reaches it. The game's PWA caches them as `/media/**`.
- `nx serve angular-examples` only serves the shell. Use `nx run angular-examples:serve-all` to boot the shell plus all remotes (ports 4200-4203).

## Cloud Functions (Bacteria Wars)

- `apps/bacteria-wars-functions` is the game's server code (ADR 0011, 0012): 2nd-gen functions, codebase `bacteria` in `firebase.bacteria-game-remote.json`, region `REGION` in `src/config.ts` (the Firestore location of `bacteria-wars`). It takes the engine from `@wolsok/feat-shared-bacteria-engine` (`libs/features/bacteria-engine`, tag `feat-shared`, Node-only: no Angular, NgRx, RxJS, Firebase or DOM) and bundles it (`@nx/esbuild`, ESM, `thirdParty: false`); `firebase-admin` and `firebase-functions` stay external, at the versions in the app's own `package.json`, which a spec keeps equal to the workspace's.
- The documents the functions write and the game and the admin read are described once, in the engine's `state/cloud/records/`: the ban (`parseBan(data, toMillis)`, `banHolds`, end exclusive as the rules' `notBanned()`, and the Realtime Database mirror `mirroredBan`/`parseMirroredBan`), notice types, replay kinds and states, hide reasons, the admin statistics' figures and whether a stored replay plays back (`storedPlaybackRefusal` on `StoredPlayback`, which every writer stores through `storedPlaybackOf` and which "My matches" and the gallery's `fitsGallery` ask instead of a check of their own). Each side passes its own Timestamp mapping (`timestampMillis` in the functions' `src/timestamps.ts`, `millisOf` in the game and the admin); the admin takes them through `admin-kit`. A new shape both sides read goes there too.
- The client never calls a function: it writes command documents (`replaySubmissions`, `replayCommands`) that triggers process. Triggers run with retries off and are idempotent (`create()` or a transaction checks first).
- A command document's envelope (`uid`, `createdAt`, `expireAt` a day ahead: `COMMAND_ENVELOPE_KEYS`, `COMMAND_TTL_MS`), the replay command types, `parseReplayCommand` and the result (`CommandResult`, `{ ok, error?, at }`, `parseCommandResult`) live in the engine's `state/cloud/command-documents.ts`; the game and the admin write the envelope with `commandEnvelope` (game lib `storage/command-envelope.ts`, in the admin kit). In the functions, `runCommandDocument` (`src/commands/run-command-document.ts`) checks that the writer is the command's `uid`, turns a throw into `internal` and writes `result` back; `runAdminCommand` and `runReplayCommand` keep only what their commands do, and a new command collection runs through it too.
- The boards (`src/boards/`) are written by functions only: entries carry no uid (`boardMembers/{uid}.entryIds` maps them), `rebuildTop` alone writes a board's top document, and every composite query has its index checked by `indexes.spec.ts` against `firestore.indexes.json`, since the emulator enforces none.
- `test` runs the pure specs; `test-emulator` runs `*.emulator.ts` against the Firestore emulator on ports of its own (`emulator.json`). Each emulator spec takes its `db` from `useEmulatorDb()` (`src/testing/emulator.ts`, which starts the app once and clears the ban cache and Firestore before each test, on the project `test-emulator` names) and its Realtime Database from the one fake, `fakeRealtime()` (`src/testing/fake-realtime.ts`: a tree like the real one, with a log of what was written in `calls`, a hook-free `peek`, `failRemoving` and race hooks); `src/testing/` is test code, kept out of `tsconfig.app.json`. The game's rules are tested the same way in `apps/bacteria-game-remote/rules-test` (`bacteria-game-remote:test-emulator`). CI runs both targets.
- Errors go to the Sentry project `bacteria-wars-functions` (`src/error-reports.ts`, DSN `SENTRY_DSN` in `src/config.ts`): `main.ts` calls `initErrorReports()`, which starts `@sentry/node` only in a deployed function (`K_SERVICE` set, not the emulator or Jest), and wraps every exported handler in `withSentry(handler)`, which captures, waits for `flush` and rethrows, so retries stay as they were. A new function gets the wrapper too; handler modules stay free of Sentry. `@sentry/node` is external and in the app's `package.json` at the workspace's version (`package-json.spec.ts`).
- Handler modules import `firebase-functions/logger`, not `firebase-functions`: the root export loads the admin auth stack, which Jest on Node 22 cannot require.
- Re-running a replay (`boards/verify.ts`, judged by the engine's `replayVerdict`: `verified`, `unverified`, `balance-mismatch` or `unplayable`, the last stored as `unverified`) costs real CPU: `gpu-int`, the only ruleset ranked attempts take, played at about 7 ms a tick on `intSimulation` before #3065 made it about 2-2.8x faster (bench and large map; the server is not measured again), so a 10-minute match still takes a minute or more. Specs never replay whole matches: `verifyDailySlice` takes the verifier as a parameter, and `verify.spec.ts` mocks `replayVerdict`. `playReplay`, the balance lab, the replay viewer (`ReplayScene`) and the CPU bench play a match through the engine's `MatchRun` (`state/match/match-run.ts`: arena, last tick, frame deadline, seek, result with checksum); a new loop that plays a match on without a player uses it too, never its own `engine.tick` loop. The live match still ticks in `GameStateService.advance`. Firestore holds no arrays in arrays; flatten what a function stores.
- `hourly` (`boards/hourly.ts`) is exported only with `HOURLY_ON` in `src/config.ts`; set it to `false` to take it out of a deploy.
- `featureBest` (`gallery/feature-best.ts`, the gallery's daily pick into `publicReplays`) is exported only with `FEATURE_BEST_ON` in `src/config.ts`, on since the gallery's pages and the Replays view of `/admin` shipped (ADR 0011 rollout step 6); set it to `false` to take it out of a deploy.
- Account deletion erases the player's data (ADR 0012, owner's decisions of 2026-10-26). Where that data lives is one table, `PLAYER_DATA` (`src/erasure/player-data.ts`): every collection, document and Realtime Database node with the part that erases it and how (`doc`, `tree`, `field`, `node` by path or field; `custom` by the part's own code; `keep` with its reason), and `player-data.spec.ts` fails on a `match` path of `firestore.rules` or a node of `database.rules.json` without an entry, on a path listed twice or below a `tree`. A new collection or node of a player gets its entry there, and its erasing too. `erasePart(part, ctx, uid)` (`src/erasure/erase.ts`) is the one entry point of the three `auth.user().onDelete` triggers: `account` for `deletePlayerBoards` (`admin/accounts.ts`: boards, pairs, bans, audit and the owner's commands about the player, count), `social` for `deletePlayerData` (`social/delete-player.ts`: `players/{uid}/**`, profile, the player in other players' lists, queue, open rooms, invites, presence and both mirrors) and `replays` for `deletePlayerReplays`, which no longer deletes replays: `replays/forget.ts` takes the uid out of `players`, seats, `optOut` and `reports`, and the replay stays for the statistics until its `expireAt` (none while still public). Each part deletes its plain entries through `eraseListed` where its order needs it (`replays` first, its pending `replaySubmissions` and `replayCommands`; `account` and `social` after their reads); `acceptReplay` reads its submission in its slot and store transactions and drops one that is gone (`withdrawn`), so taking the slot marks the submission (`slotTaken`) rather than deleting it. `erasePlayer` runs every part; `erasure/erasure.emulator.ts` tests the erasure, table-driven for the plain entries.
- `guestCleanup` (`admin/guests.ts`, daily at 03:41 UTC) deletes guest accounts (no provider) unused for `GUEST_IDLE_DAYS` (90); exported only with `GUEST_CLEANUP_ON`, on together with the friends-only status rule, which ships only after "Mirror friend lists" (`presence.backfill`) has run once in production. Auth's bulk `deleteUsers` fires no `onDelete`, so it runs `erasePlayer` (`erasure/erase.ts`) for each guest first and deletes the account only once that succeeded. It lowers `stats/accounts` once a batch by the decrements its erases claimed (`accountCounted` cleared in a transaction, so each account counts down once), never once a guest.
- The friend lists are mirrored into the Realtime Database by `mirrorFriend` and `mirrorRequest` (`social/mirror.ts`): `statusReaders/{owner}/{reader}` (for the coming friends-only read rule of `status/{owner}`) and `listedBy/{uid}/{owner}/{friends|requests}` (where the deletion finds the player in others' lists). Functions only: the database rules close both to clients. Both triggers retry; each re-reads the entry after its write and writes again if it changed, so out-of-order events end right. Ids the Realtime Database takes as no key (`isRealtimeKey` in `admin/realtime.ts`) are skipped everywhere, and the Firestore rules take only uid-shaped ids in `friends`, `requests` and `challenges`. The admin command `presence.backfill` adds what is missing and removes entries without a list entry.
- The player's replay command `forget` ("Delete" in "My matches", `replays/forget.ts`) takes them out of the replay and its public copies; allowed while banned, like every deletion, and refused (`ranking`) while the boards may still rank the match, an online match still `waiting` for its second report included (`stillRanking` in `replays/forget-plan.ts`).
- Its `deploy` target (`firebase deploy --config=firebase.bacteria-game-remote.json --only functions:bacteria --force`) calls the Firebase CLI itself, not `nx run bacteria-game-remote:firebase`: the game's hosting deploy ran that task in the same release, and the second, nested run of it failed every functions deploy. It runs in the `non-cdk` leg of `deploy.yml` whenever a release affects the app, which includes every change to the game's engine (`feat-shared-bacteria-engine`), since the app imports it. `--force` deletes functions of the `bacteria` codebase that are gone from `main.ts`, so taking a function out of the exports takes it out of production. The game's hosting deploy leaves the functions alone (`--only hosting,firestore,database`). It runs `firebase deploy` through `tools/deploy/retry-once.ts` (`tsx --tsconfig tools/tsconfig.tools.json`, project `tools-deploy`), which reruns a failed command once after 30 s, so a single transient error of Google's API no longer fails the release; the healed failure stays visible as a `::warning::`, a second failure fails the deploy. The retry decision is `runWithOneRetry` (`tools/deploy/run-with-one-retry.ts`), spec'd in `tools-deploy:test`. `korbjaeger:deploy` and `korbjaeger-functions:deploy` run every Firebase CLI call through it too (#2946), and so do the Hosting deploys of `pacetrainer`, `rollapolla-analog` and `bacteria-game-remote` (#3034), each calling `firebase --config=firebase.<app>.json --project=<app> deploy … --non-interactive` itself rather than a nested `nx run <app>:firebase`; `tools/deploy/deploy-targets.spec.ts` holds every Hosting deploy to that call and to no `nx` command. A new function or Hosting deploy does the same. The helper is CommonJS under tsx (the root `package.json` has no `"type": "module"`), so it uses no top-level `await`.
- Every Firebase Hosting deploy ends with `tools/deploy/check-live-index.ts <firebase-config> <public URL>` (#3073), which fetches `/` for up to two minutes until it serves, byte for byte, the built `index.html` of the config's `hosting.public`, and else fails the release, since a deploy once reported success with the previous release still live (#3058); `tools/deploy/deploy-targets.spec.ts` keeps it on the deploy of every root `firebase.<app>.json` with `hosting` and fails on one whose public domain it does not know.
- Every Firebase `predeploy` that runs `npm install` for a function (`firebase.bacteria-game-remote.json`, `firebase.pacetrainer.json`, `firebase.rollapolla-analog.json`) passes `--legacy-peer-deps=false`: deploys run inside `npx nx`, which exports the root `.npmrc` as `npm_config_legacy_peer_deps=true`, and the lock written that way lacks required peers, so Cloud Build's `npm ci` refuses it (`Missing: … from lock file`). A spec in each app keeps the flag (`package-json.spec.ts`, `firebase-deploy.spec.ts`); a new function config gets both.

## Android App

- `apps/bacteria-wars-android` is a Gradle project, not a web build: a Trusted Web Activity that opens `https://bacteria-wars.wolsok.de` (the `bacteria-game-remote` PWA) fullscreen in Chrome. Game changes go into the PWA; the app picks them up with the next web deploy.
- Its Nx targets are `apk`, `bundle`, `lint-android` and `deploy`, deliberately not `build`/`lint`/`test`: the Nx Cloud workers have no Android SDK. The `Android app` GitHub workflow (`.github/workflows/android.yml`) builds and lints it on PRs instead. `deploy` signs the release, attaches the APK and bundle to the GitHub release and uploads the bundle to Play's closed testing track (`alpha`); the `android` leg of `deploy.yml` runs it when a release affects the app. See its `README.md` for signing and Play.
- Fullscreen depends on `apps/bacteria-game-remote/src/.well-known/assetlinks.json` naming the app's package and signing-key fingerprints. Gradle reads the package name from that file, so it is the one place to change it; the host is set in `app/build.gradle.kts` and served by Firebase Hosting (`firebase.bacteria-game-remote.json`).
- Launcher icons and splash come from `npx nx run bacteria-game-remote:icons`; don't edit the PNGs by hand.
- `store/` holds what Play shows: the listing texts and graphics, the promo videos and, in `store/play-games/achievements/`, the Play Games Services achievement icons (`npx nx run bacteria-wars-android:achievement-icons`). The achievements themselves are the game's: `play-games-achievements.json` in `libs/features/bacteria-engine/src/lib/state/progress/`, with its spec keeping it in line with the game's achievements. The deploy syncs them to Play as drafts (`tools/bacteria-game/play-games.ts`); the Publish page in Play Console takes them live. Game details and graphics of the Play Games project are the store listing's, entered by hand.
- `app/google-services.json` registers the app with the Firebase project `bacteria-wars` (the `google-services` Gradle plugin, Firebase Analytics, with the advertising id permission removed in the manifest); the Android OAuth client Play Games Services needs lives on that Firebase app. Its `project_number` is also the Play Games Services game id: Gradle puts it into `game_services_project_id` for the manifest's `APP_ID`, the deploy reads it for the achievement sync, and `BacteriaWarsApplication` starts the Play Games SDK, which signs the player in silently on launch. The game itself (in Chrome) cannot reach that SDK; unlocking achievements from the web is still open. The privacy policy (`apps/bacteria-game-remote/src/app/privacy`) names Analytics and the Play Games sign-in; keep it in step with what the app does.
- `tools/bacteria-game/dish.ts` holds the colony palette and the petri dish both icon generators draw with; change colours there.
- Tips and ads live in the game lib's `support/` folder and are switched on by `provideGameSupport` in the remote's app config only, so the shell shows neither. On the web the game links to Buy Me a Coffee; in the app it sells Play tips instead (Play allows no other donation link). Ads come from a network behind the `AdNetwork` port (`support/ads/`, ADR 0017): `GameAds` loads the adapter `support.ads.network` names in `environment.prod.ts` (`adinplay` or `adsense`), whose script brings the network's consent banner; without `support.ads` the game loads no ad script at all, as on the live site until AdinPlay takes it. A new network is an adapter of its own, never a special case in a screen. Keep interstitials and auto ads off, or ads cover the game. The privacy policy's section 7 is rendered per network (`GameAds.networkName`); a new one gets its text there. The shared tip settings are in `environments/game-support.ts`. Changes to them belong into the privacy policy (`src/app/privacy`) too.

## Korbjäger (basketball parents app)

- `apps/korbjaeger` (prefix `korb`, German UI, `korb.wolsok.de` in `SITE_URL` of `src/shared/site.ts`) is an Analog app on the Nitro `firebase` preset with `ssr: false`: pages render in the browser, Nitro serves the shell and the DBB proxy.
- It deploys to the Firebase project `korbjaeger`, named only in `.firebaserc` (alias `korbjaeger`): its `deploy` target (`firebase.korbjaeger.json`, in the `non-cdk` leg of `deploy.yml`) puts the build on the project's default Hosting site, which `korbjaeger-cdk` (stack `Korbjaeger`, `cdk` leg) names as `KORBJAEGER_HOSTING_SITE`, checked against `.firebaserc` by its spec, for the CNAME `korb.wolsok.de` → `<site>.web.app`. Hosting rewrites only `/api/**` to the Nitro function (`europe-central2`, at most 10 instances, in `vite.config.ts`) and every path without a file extension to `/index.html` (every extension-less path outside `/api/`, unknown ones too, and `/index.html` sent `no-cache`, the paths by three glob rules (`/`, `/!(api|*.*)`, `/!(api)/**/!(*.*)`) that `firebase-deploy.spec.ts` checks with Hosting's own matcher (superstatic's `configMatcher`, a devDependency for it); never `/api/**`, since Hosting's header rules override the function's `Cache-Control`; a chunk a release removed is a 404, not the shell), so pages come from the CDN; Nitro's generated `apps/korbjaeger/firebase.json` is not what deploys. The stack keeps its own `KORBJAEGER_DOMAIN`, since infra may import no app, and its spec keeps it equal to `SITE_URL`; `firebase-deploy.spec.ts` keeps the config (rewrites, `--legacy-peer-deps=false`). The web config is in `src/environments/environment.ts` (`environmentFor(mode)`); its spec keeps `projectId` equal to `.firebaserc`. The deploy puts the Firestore rules (`apps/korbjaeger/firestore.rules`) and indexes (`firestore.indexes.json`, the tombstones' TTL) live with the app (`--only functions:default,hosting,firestore:rules,firestore:indexes`, kept by `firebase-deploy.spec.ts`): the Nitro server is codebase `default` of `firebase.korbjaeger.json`, codebase `konto` is `korbjaeger-functions`'.
- The screens read `BasketballData` from `@wolsok/feat-shared-basketball-data` (`libs/features/basketball-data`, tag `feat-shared`, no Angular, Firebase, RxJS or DOM), whose `DbbBasketballData` maps the DBB's undocumented JSON API (ADR 0018). The browser's transport (`src/app/basketball-data/`) calls the app's proxy, since the DBB sends no CORS headers; the `BASKETBALL_DATA` token is typed `KorbjaegerData`, the reads the proxy has a route for, so a read without one does not compile. Spiel questions (home or away, opponent, result, cancelled or forfeited) are the lib's domain helpers; the app only formats.
- The app is a PWA: `src/public/manifest.webmanifest`, icons from `npx nx run korbjaeger:icons` (`tools/korbjaeger/generate-icons.ts`; never by hand) and Angular's service worker (`ngsw-config.json`, `provideAppServiceWorker` in `src/app/pwa/`, production builds only). `build` is `build-app` (Analog, cached; `serve`/`serve-e2e` build through it) followed by `ngsw-config` on `dist/apps/korbjaeger/analog/public`, never cached (`ngsw.json` hashes `build-app`'s files). The worker caches the shell only, never `/api/**` (no data group; `navigationUrls` leave `/api` to the network, `src/pwa/service-worker.spec.ts`); a new server path gets the same exclusion.
- The home page suggests installing the app (`korb-install-hint`, which only displays `InstallHint` in `src/app/pwa/install-hint.ts`, started by `provideInstallHint` so it hears an early `beforeinstallprompt`; the decision is the pure `installOffer`): "Installieren" (the event's `prompt()`) where the browser fires it, the way through the share menu on iOS where no `beforeinstallprompt` came (`isIosWithShareMenu`: Safari, other iOS browsers from iOS 16.4, never an app's web view: no `Safari/` token, or the Google app, Facebook, Instagram), the browser's own install offer left alone (no `preventDefault`) unless a page shows the hint (`show`), nothing where the app runs installed (`display-mode: standalone`, `navigator.standalone`) or was dismissed ("Ausblenden", kept as `korbjaeger-install-dismissed` in `localStorage` where the device lets it, else for the visit).
- The browser transport keeps the last good answer of a Team's Spiele, a Tabelle, a Spiel's match info and a Verein's Spiele per proxy path in `localStorage` (`STORABLE_KINDS` in `src/app/basketball-data/proxy-transport.ts`; the store `LocalAnswerCache` and its upkeep `maintainAnswerCache` are the lib `feat-korbjaeger-answers` (`libs/features/korbjaeger-answers`, tag `feature`, no Angular, behind the storage port `AnswerStorage`, #2930), which the app's `ANSWER_CACHE` token wires; `isStorageFull` for both it and `LocalSelection` is `@wolsok/utils-browser-storage`): without the persons it names (the lib's `dbbWithoutPersons`), never a Spielbericht or the Liga search (ADR 0019), only once the adapter mapped it (the read's `Reading` in `KorbReadOptions`, typed through `DbbBasketballData<O>`), at most 7 days old (cleared at start, on returning to the page and hourly: `ANSWER_CACHE`), capped at 60 answers and 1,000,000 characters with an index (oldest evicted once the new one is stored, quota errors evict too, an answer not kept drops the older one of its path); they give way when Meine Teams find the storage full (`FREE_STORAGE`). A read that fails as `offline` or `unavailable` is answered from it; the resource's `asOf` (a `DataResource`) tells the screens, each card or section showing the oldest of its reads in `korb-as-of` ("Stand: vor …", on the `NOW` clock in `src/app/now.ts`; `TODAY` derives from it). `offline` (fetch throws, no answer within `PROXY_TIMEOUT_MS`, or `navigator.onLine` false as `NoInternetError`, the only case worded "Kein Internet"/"Offline"), `unavailable` (502) and `not-found` (404) each have their text in `src/app/errors/`.
- The proxy (`src/server/routes/api/dbb/`, thin, over `src/server/dbb/`) serves only what the lib's `dbbHttpRequest` allowlists, one route per read with numeric ids (`parseDbbId`); the Liga search (`/api/dbb/ligen`, `/api/dbb/ligen/seite`) is a GET with its filter in the query string, from which the proxy builds the DBB's POST body (unknown parameters 404); every other path under `/api/dbb/` is 404. It passes the DBB body on unchanged; `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, s-maxage=300` on success only (a boxscore with a confirmed result and both Kader `s-maxage=3600`, decided from the body by the lib's `dbbBoxscoreFinished`, no second DBB call; unconfirmed stays at 300), every error `no-store` (else Hosting adds `max-age=600`), DBB `status:"1"` → 404, timeout, network error, 5xx or `status:"-1"` → 502; its own User-Agent, no cookies either way. `src/shared/dbb-proxy-routes.ts` maps each read to its URL (`urlOf`) and a route's params and query back to the read (`readOf`), for transport and proxy alike; a new read gets its entry there, its route file, its place in `KorbjaegerData` and its specs. The DBB's base URL is Nitro runtime config (`dbbBaseUrl`, `NITRO_DBB_BASE_URL` at run time). Nitro doesn't read tsconfig paths; `vite.config.ts` gives it the `@wolsok/*` aliases through `tools/vite/nitro-ts-path-aliases.ts`.
- Meine Teams and the marked Kinder go through the `Selection` port (the lib `feat-korbjaeger-selection`, `libs/features/korbjaeger-selection`, tag `feature`, #2917: port, document, changes, both adapters, takeover and the contract under `@wolsok/feat-korbjaeger-selection` and `/testing`; the app keeps the token `SELECTION` in `src/app/selection/selection.ts` and the emulator specs, and imports only the lib's entries; token `SELECTION`: `teams` and `children` signals, `undefined` until read, with `follow`/`unfollow` and `mark`/`setNickname`/`unmark`), whose local adapter `LocalSelection` keeps `{ version: 3, teams, children, clubColors }` under `korbjaeger-selection` (`selection-document.ts`, each list read, diffed, merged, joined and signalled by its descriptor in `LIST_DESCRIPTORS` (`selection-lists.ts`, the descriptors in `lists/`, #2928), so a new list is a descriptor, a cap and its rules, not edits across the adapters: the maps keyed by DBB id, `teams: { [id]: since }`, `children: { [personId]: { since, nickname? } }`, ordered by `since`, and `clubColors: { [vereinId]: '#rrggbb' | '#rrggbb,#rrggbb' }` (#2918, `setClubColors`/`resetClubColors` on the port; the colours in lower case, `colorsText`/`colorsFromText` in the lib's `club-colors-choice.ts`, `NotAColorError` in its `club-colors.ts`), by Verein id; version 3 (#2966) names the fields in English; the German versions 1 and 2 are read as none, as #2983 removed their migration) in `localStorage`, re-read before each write, which it stores within the call (so leaving the page right after keeps it), and on the `storage` event (two tabs), keeping unknown fields and writing only the parts a change touched; a change no write could store (storage full or blocked) stays `pending`, applied on top of what is read until a write takes it; unreadable or foreign data counts as empty (malformed `children` alone as no Kinder, the Teams kept), a newer version is left alone and changes rejected with `SelectionTooNewError`. A Kind is `{ personId, nickname? }` only (`child.ts`: the Spitzname trimmed, at most 30 characters, empty as none), never a name; `mark` takes a `MarkablePlayer`, which only a named player (`NamedPlayer`) is, so an Anonymer Spieler cannot be marked. Every adapter runs the shared contract suite `selectionContract` (the lib's `testing/selection-contract.ts`), `FirestoreSelection` against the emulator; the change functions both apply are `selection-changes.ts`, and every writer (both adapters and the takeover) writes what `selectionFields` gives: only the entries a change adds, removes or whose Spitzname it changes; specs that need an `Selection` that misbehaves take `fakeSelection` (the lib's `testing/fake-selection.ts`).
- Signing in with Google is optional (#2873, ADR 0019) and live in production (`environment.signIn` is set in every mode; development, e2e and the specs sign in against the emulators), covered by the privacy policy (below). The Firestore database is in `europe-west3` (Frankfurt), the Nitro function in `europe-central2` (both `REGIONS` in `src/shared/regions.ts`: the function's `FUNCTION_REGION` from the import-free `src/shared/function-region.ts`, which `vite.config.ts` deploys it by, since a Vite config resolves no `@wolsok/*` alias, and `FIRESTORE_REGION` from `@wolsok/feat-shared-korbjaeger-account`): a function that reads or writes Firestore belongs in `europe-west3`. `ACCOUNT_SESSION` (`src/app/account/account.ts`, `AccountSession`) holds the account and hands `SELECTION` whichever `Selection` holds the choices: `LocalSelection` signed out, `FirestoreSelection` (`selections/{uid}`, Firestore's persistent cache, so offline too) signed in, `undefined` teams while it switches; `unreadable` (on the port) says the account could not be read, and the overview says so. `FirestoreSelection` writes each change as those entries, merged (`setDoc` with `merge`, `deleteField()` for one that goes, `firestoreFields`), online and offline alike (no network check, no transaction), so the server merges it with other devices' changes entry by entry; it resolves once on the device and shows on top of the listener's state until the server answered; a refused write (a cap another device filled: the rules refuse, never cut; a Spitzname for a Kind unmarked meanwhile, which has no `since`) is taken back by Firestore. After a listener error, or `stop`, it shows nothing (`undefined`) and refuses every change. A device acts on what it has seen; a document without `teams` reads as no Teams, its Kinder kept. Firebase sits behind the `AccountService` port (`account-service.ts`); `FirebaseAccountService` is its own chunk, imported only once the settings open (so a click opens Google's popup without waiting, which Safari requires, and "Mit Google anmelden" stays disabled, saying it is getting ready, until the chunk is loaded (`AccountSession.ready`); the delete dialog starts the deletion in its click for the same reason) or to reopen the account of an Elternteil signed in before (`korbjaeger-signed-in` in `localStorage`), so a visitor who never opens the settings never contacts Google; the service worker caches it lazily and fetches its updates ahead (group `account` in `ngsw-config.json`, `service-worker.spec.ts`). Every tab follows a sign-in or sign-out in another (Auth's state, and the `storage` event of `korbjaeger-signed-in` before Firebase is loaded), and a tab whose account's document the rules refuse (signed out or deleted elsewhere) signs out. Every sign-in takes the device's choices into the account (`takeOverDevice`: `mergeSelections`, the account's first, its Spitzname winning, the device's only up to the caps; one transaction a map) and then those the account took off the device (`LocalSelection.handOver`, one read and write, so what did not fit stays on the device and what joined meanwhile in any tab goes over in another round, up to three); the session tells the account shown what the takeover left (`takeoverHint`: the entries that did not fit, and `kept` where new ones still wait for the next start), and a start takes kept choices over as a step of its own (`take-over`, so no deletion runs meanwhile), the account open even where that fails; only that takeover ever clears the device's choices, never a sign-out (here or followed from another tab, after a failed takeover too); a failed takeover signs out and clears the cache; once a sign-in, sign-out or deletion ends, the session reconciles with Auth's current user (another tab may have signed out meanwhile); the latest opening of an account wins (a newer one or a sign-out supersedes it, it checks Auth's user before showing, a failed one shows `unreachable` and Auth's next word opens it again, and a start that found nobody signed in gives way to one meanwhile), and it hides the previous one's choices first; the step running and the last one's failure are the session's (`running`, `failure`), so settings opened again show them; a start signed out clears the cache a sign-out left (`korbjaeger-clear-cache`; the device flags and their keys are in `src/app/device-storage.ts`, `isFlagSet`/`setFlag`; `main.ts` first removes the keys of before #2966, carrying only the signed-in and clear-cache flags over, `dropKeysBeforeEnglishNames` in `src/app/keys-before-english-names.ts`); one sign-in, sign-out or deletion runs at a time; signing out waits for the device's changes to reach the account (refused with `NotAllSentError` where they don't within seconds), signs out of Auth, then terminates Firestore and clears its cache (`clearCache`, which never rejects: where it fails or another tab holds the cache, at the next start); deleting the account (`/einstellungen`, `src/app/account/settings.component.ts`, with a confirm dialog) asks Google again first, is refused offline (`NoInternetToDeleteError`), then deletes `selections/{uid}`, waiting for the server's confirmation however long it takes (the settings say it runs; a queued delete runs anyway), and only then the Auth user, both by the uid Google was asked about (`AccountSwitchedError` where another tab switched accounts meanwhile; `AccountNotDeletedError` where Auth then refuses, so deleting again finishes it; a document another device recreates meanwhile is deleted by `deleteSelection`, below). The settings offer the sign-in again (`Erneut versuchen`) where Firebase's chunk could not be loaded. The name shown is Auth's, kept in memory only. The caps are `SELECTION_LIMITS` (`selection-lists.ts`: 50 Teams, 20 Kinder, the colours of 50 Vereine): both adapters refuse a change over them with `SelectionFullError`, and the Firestore rules (`firestore.rules`, whose spec takes the same numbers) take only `version` (3), `teams` (DBB ids to an int `since`), `clubColors` (Verein ids to their colour text, all values checked at once by one regular expression over `values().join(";")`, as a check per entry takes more expressions than 50 allow) and `children` (person ids to an int `since` and an optional `nickname`, text of at most `NICKNAME_CODE_POINTS` (330) code points, which `nicknameOf` keeps to as well beside its 30 characters) up to them, only from the owner; the keys as DBB ids of at most 15 digits in one regular expression over `keys().join(",")` (as many parts as keys, so none holds a comma), the values by index, an update that only removes entries as it is (a map over its cap shrinks); a request may evaluate at most 1000 expressions, too few for both maps full, so a create checks both and an update only the maps it changes, and the app changes one map a write. `deploy` takes only a production build: Nx hands `-c development` on to `build`, so `build-app` records the mode it built in with its artifacts (`rememberBuildConfiguration`, a Vite plugin in `apps/korbjaeger/deploy/build-configuration.ts`, an output of `build-app`, so its cache brings it too), and the deploy's first command refuses any other (`firebase-deploy.spec.ts`). `test-emulator` runs `src/**/*.emulator.ts` (the rules, the contract on `FirestoreSelection`, the merge; helpers in `src/testing/firestore-emulator.ts`) on the Firestore emulator of `emulator/firebase.test.json`; `test-emulator` runs as project `demo-korbjaeger-test`, apart from `emulatoren` (continuous, `firebase.emulatoren.json`, project `demo-korbjaeger`), since two emulator suites of one project id on one machine (an Nx Cloud agent) share the Firebase CLI's hub locator; `emulatoren` runs Auth and Firestore for `nx serve korbjaeger` and the e2e, which signs in through the Auth emulator's popup (`e2e/account.spec.ts`, without a fixed clock: Auth's tokens carry the real time) on Chromium's new headless mode (`channel: 'chromium'`; in the headless shell the emulator's helper frame now and then never parses, leaving the popup open).

The overview (`src/app/overview/`) asks the lib's `teamOverview`, `combinedOverview` (several Teams together, for a Kind) and `byNextGame` (next Spiel: the first still `scheduled`; cancelled or forfeited ones before it; last result; order) and only formats. A Kind's card shows what falls through in tip-off order around its next Spiel (`combinedOverview`'s `cancellations` and `laterCancellations`), names the Team of its next Spiel and last result where it has several, and says when another Team's Spiele or Spielberichte could not all be read. While no Kind is marked, every Team shows as before, with a hint how to mark one (after the first Spiel, or on a played Spiel's page). `FollowedTeamsOverview` only wires the overview; the reads per followed Team are `teamReadings` (`team-readings.ts`: each Team's `teamOverview` in a computed of its own, `TeamReadings.overview`, for its card and its Kind; its Saison through `teamSeasonResource`, as the Team page, and, once its next Spiel is known, that Spiel's details for the Halle through `gameDetailsResource`, both in `src/app/basketball-data/`), reconciled with Meine Teams by `reconcile`; the last Kader finds are kept by the pure `roster-finds.ts`, a Team as the overview holds it is built by `teamInOverview`, and the cards only show what they are given. The Spiel page (`src/app/game-page/`) reads the Spiel and its Spielbericht on their own and formats through pure view models; domain questions (`playerStatsRecorded`, `fieldGoals`, `isNamed`) stay in the lib. The Team page lists the Verein's other Teams (`clubTeams`, the club's Spiele of `CLUB_GAMES_DAYS` either way, fixed in the read, never a client parameter) with the follow control (`src/app/club/`); a Team whose Saison looks over (the lib's `seasonOver`: no Spiel left, the last more than two weeks past) gets a hint that asks rather than claims (a break looks the same) and suggests them, `SeasonOverHintComponent` on its Team page and its overview card; the overview reads each such Verein only then, once.

## Testing

- **Unit (Jest)**: colocated as `<file>.spec.ts`; mock external services; keep fast and deterministic
- **Spec typecheck**: Jest transpiles without type checking, so fakes and calls in specs drift from the real types unnoticed. A project whose specs must typecheck gets an empty `"typecheck-specs": {}` target (command `tsc -p {projectRoot}/tsconfig.spec.json --noEmit`, inputs and caching from `targetDefaults` in `nx.json`), which CI runs among the affected targets; `feat-lazy-bacteria-game` has one. Not the same as the `typecheck` target `@nx/vite` infers for some projects, which checks the lib or app sources, not the specs
- **Unit (Vitest)**: used in Vite-based projects (check `project.json` for the `@nx/vitest` plugin / `@nx/vitest:test` executor)
- **E2E (Playwright)**: in `apps/<app>/e2e/`; page objects in `e2e/pos/`, fixtures in `e2e/fixtures/`
  - Start every `webServer` through an Nx target (`npx nx serve <app>`, `npx nx run <app>:<target>` for a `continuous` target) with `reuseExistingServer: true`. Inside an Nx task, Nx starts those targets, not Playwright: Nx stops and restarts continuous tasks between the batches an Nx Cloud agent runs, so a spec can find its servers still booting after the `--wait-for-webserver` gate already ran elsewhere, and a second start from Playwright fails on the taken ports ("Process from config.webServer exited early"). So every such entry comes from `nxServer(target, url, { cwd, timeout })` (`@wolsok/shared-e2e-server`, `libs/shared/e2e-server`), whose command only waits for the URL (`src/wait-for-server.mjs`) where `NX_TASK_TARGET_PROJECT` is set; the plugin still infers the dependency from the `nx run` command, read outside a task. Only then does `@nx/playwright` make the atomized `e2e-ci--*` tasks depend on those servers and wait for them, so several spec files on one Nx Cloud worker share them. A server Playwright starts itself clashes with the next spec file on the same worker (see `rollapolla-analog`). A static server (`@nx/web:file-server`) serves `staticFilePath` and `dependsOn: ["build"]` with `watch: false`, not a `buildTarget`: with `buildTarget` it runs a nested `nx build`, which Nx refuses as a recursive task invocation inside a shared run. Exception for now: `angular-examples` (the federation shell, one spec file) still lets Playwright start its server in CI; with the inferred serve dependency its page did not render on the Nx Cloud workers, while it passed locally.
- **Emulators on the Nx Cloud workers**: the workers download the Firebase emulators (`npx firebase setup:emulators:<name>`) in an init step of `.nx/workflows/workers.yml`, after `npm install` and before any task: the CLI otherwise downloads one on first use with a non-atomic copy, and a second emulator task on the same worker started Java on the partial jar and failed within seconds (#2960). A Firebase config using a new downloadable emulator (`pubsub`, `storage`, `dataconnect`; the UI unless `ui.enabled` is `false`) gets its step there; `tools/ci/nx-cloud-workers.test.mjs` (`npx nx test tools`) fails without it, on an inline init script (`script:`) not starting with POSIX `set -eu` (#3067: Nx Cloud documents neither the shell nor fail-fast, and `pipefail` would fail every step under dash), and when `stop-after` in `.nx/ci-config.yaml` differs from the targets of `ci-cd.yml`'s `nx affected -t` call
- **Deploy inputs name the root Firebase config literally** (#2904): a project whose targets pass a root `firebase.<x>.json` to the Firebase CLI lists `{workspaceRoot}/firebase.<x>.json` among its `deploy` inputs, so a change to the config makes it affected and the next release redeploys it. Never `{projectName}` in an input: Nx interpolates it in commands only, and such an input matches no file. `tools/ci/deploy-inputs.test.mjs` (`npx nx test tools`, which runs every `tools/**/*.test.mjs`, `tools/firebase/grant-admin.test.mjs` included) fails on either; `tools/ci/target-inputs.test.mjs` fails on any target input `{workspaceRoot}/<file>` (no glob), string or `fileset`, naming a file that does not exist, in a `project.json` or `nx.json`, and on a `{projectRoot}/<file>` one in a `project.json` (its targets and its `namedInputs`), resolved against its folder (#2946, #3051); since a renamed file makes only its own project affected, never `tools`, `ci-cd.yml` also runs it on every run as the uncached step "Target inputs name existing files" (`node --test`, outside Nx, with no `if:` or `continue-on-error`), which the test keeps
- **What a release deploys** (#2888): `deploy.yml` and the release trigger in `ci-cd.yml` select through `tools/ci/release-affected.mjs`, which keeps a project Nx calls affected only when a changed file is an input of its `deploy` task (a published package: its `build`) or of a task it depends on, as `nx run --graph` and `nx show target inputs` resolve them; Nx alone counts every target's inputs, so a lint-only root config (`.oxlintrc.json`, `eslint.config.mjs`) redeployed every app. A paths-only `tsconfig.base.json` change counts as the files its aliases point to (one touching a wildcard alias or target, or a target that is no file at base or head, such as a directory, as the base itself, #3041; targets count normalised), a version-only bump of a project's `package.json` deploys no app, and a lockfile, root `package.json`, `nx.json`, root `tsconfig*.json` (the base only where no paths-only change narrowed it, #3024), file deleted outside every project, deleted `project.json` or unreadable input keeps Nx's verdict; a file deleted inside a project counts for that project, its dependents and the candidates whose inputs hold a file of it (longest root of `nx graph`, never the root project `.`, #3054). The legs run `nx run-many`/`nx release publish` on exactly that list, and skip on an empty one. `release-affected.test.mjs` (`npx nx test tools`) covers it. The version job of `release.yml` selects the same way (#3020): `nx release version --projects` gets only the published packages whose `build` reads a file changed since the last release `v<version.json>` (the range `ci-cd.yml`'s trigger takes, never a package's own tag, which can lag far enough behind that a deletion outside every project or a root file change keeps Nx's verdict), and the call is skipped on an empty list, since `nx release` alone counts every target's inputs too and bumped every package on a lint-only commit. A dispatch of `deploy.yml` can name the projects to deploy (`projects`, filtered per leg by `tools/ci/deploy-override.mjs`, which fails on an unknown name or one without the leg's target; a version deployed once selects nothing since its own deploy tag, and an override sets no tag) and rebuild without the Nx cache (`skip-cache`, `NX_SKIP_NX_CACHE`); `release.yml`'s call passes neither, and an existing deploy tag is left alone. Its Nx calls run with `--output-style=static`, so each deploy's Firebase output is in the log (#3058: the cached build was right, its Hosting release went missing unseen); `tools/ci/deploy-workflow.test.mjs` keeps all of it
- **GPU cross-check (Playwright, no server)**: `libs/features/bacteria-rendering/playwright.config.ts` runs the deterministic simulation's integer shaders on SwiftShader against the TypeScript reference, tick by tick (`gpu-crosscheck/`, ADR 0015). It is inferred as the `e2e-ci--*` target of `feat-bacteria-rendering` (the arena rendering and the GPU simulation, out of the game lib since #3102, tag `feature:game-kit`), so `nx affected` runs it in CI only when that lib or the engine changes, not for a change to the rest of the game. The goldens in `golden-gpu-int.json` are regenerated whenever the scenarios, the reference or the hash change; a change to what the passes compute also needs a `BALANCE_VERSION` bump, a scenario change does not; `golden.spec.ts` (Jest) recomputes them from the reference. The same check plays whole matches through the game's `gpuSimulation` (`SIM_SCENARIOS`) against `golden-gpu-sim.json`, which `sim-golden.spec.ts` keeps equal to `intSimulation`, and runs the on-device self-test; its own hashes are `SELF_TEST_GOLDEN` (the engine's `state/simulation/gpu-int/self-test-golden.ts`, with `GPU_SELF_TEST_VERSION` bumped on every change), kept in step by `self-test-golden.spec.ts`. `golden-replay.spec.ts` (in the engine lib, `libs/features/bacteria-engine/src/lib/state/replay/`) keeps a result of `golden-replay.json` per `BALANCE_VERSION` for each ruleset: `cpu` on `BacteriaSimulation`, `gpu-int` on `intSimulation`
- **Plugin E2E (Jest)**: `apps/nx-aws-cdk-v2-e2e` exercises `@wolsok/nx-aws-cdk-v2` in a generated throwaway workspace. CI runs it whenever the plugin is affected, through its `e2e-ci` target (`nx:noop`, depending on `e2e`, which holds the Jest options); run `npx nx e2e nx-aws-cdk-v2-e2e` by hand for a fast loop after changing the plugin. A test that reads a task's log runs it with `--output-style=stream` (`runNxTaskWithLogs`): without it Nx prints only its summary when stdout is no terminal
- Run `npx nx affected -t test` before pushing

## Performance Gates

Planned and phased in [ADR 0014](docs/adr/0014-performance-gates-in-ci.md); this section says what is in place. Keep it current with each phase.

- **In place, blocking** (phase 1): Angular budgets on the `production` configuration of each Angular app's `esbuild` target (`portfolio`: `build`), measured through the federation build as CI runs it. CI's `build -c=ci` falls back to `production`, so they run on every affected build and block it. Each holds a `baseline` (measured on 2026-10-26, `bacteria-game-remote`'s scripts raised on 2026-11-12 by #3047; 1 kB = 1000 bytes as Angular counts):
  - `anyScript` (the largest single script, the game's chunk in `bacteria-game-remote`) and `allScript` (all scripts, initial and lazy): warning +5%, error +10%.
  - `initial`: warning +10%, error +20%.

# CLAUDE.md — wol-sok-mono

Angular + Nx monorepo. Read this before touching anything.

## Stack

## Project Layout

apps/                   # Deployable apps
  angular-examples/     # Main showcase (Webpack + Module Federation)
  pacetrainer/          # Pace trainer (Vite + Analog.js)
  rollapolla-analog/    # Analog.js SSR demo
  *-remote/             # Module Federation remotes
  *-cdk/                # AWS CDK infra stacks
  bacteria-wars-android/ # Android app (Gradle, Trusted Web Activity)
libs/
  features/             # Domain features (can use shared + utils + ui-kit)
  shared/               # Cross-cutting concerns (can use utils)
  utils/                # Pure utilities (minimal deps)
  ui-kit/               # Reusable UI components
  public/               # Published npm packages (e.g. @wolsok/thanos)
  fib-wasm/             # WebAssembly modules
  test-helper/          # Testing utilities
tools/                  # Build/deploy node scripts
docs/                   # Architecture, testing, getting-started docs
```

## Essential Commands

```bash
# Install
npm ci

# Serve
npx nx serve pacetrainer
npx nx serve angular-examples

# Build
npx nx build <project> [--configuration production]

# Test
npx nx test <project>
npx nx run <project>:e2e

# Lint (always --fix)
npx nx lint <project> --fix            # oxlint
npx nx lint-templates <project> --fix  # angular-eslint template rules
npm run lint                          # all projects, both targets

# Format (REQUIRED before committing)
npx nx format:write

# Affected only (prefer in CI / large PRs)
npx nx affected -t build,test,lint,lint-templates

# Dependency graph
npx nx graph
```

## Engineering Principles (mandatory)

Long-term, strategic software engineering is required. A change that works but leaves the code harder to change is not done.

- **Improve the codebase with every feature and bug fix.** Leave the code you touch cleaner than you found it: extract duplication, split oversized files/functions/components, fix misleading names, remove dead code, and add missing tests around what you changed.
- **Fix root causes, not symptoms.** No workarounds or one-off special cases when the underlying design is the problem; fix the design.
- **Stay modular.** Small, focused units with one responsibility and narrow interfaces. Put logic in the right `libs/` layer (see Dependency Constraints) instead of growing app code; keep domain logic out of components and in testable services/stores/pure functions.
- **Clean Code is the standard.** Intention-revealing names, small functions, no magic values, no deep nesting, no copy-paste, single level of abstraction per function, explicit error handling.
- **Easy to maintain beats clever.** Prefer simple, readable code a newcomer can follow over terse or tricky solutions.
- **Scope of cleanup:** improvements to the code your change touches belong in the same PR. A larger refactor that the change exposes but doesn't need goes in its own PR (or an issue), so each PR stays reviewable.

## Coding Rules

1. **Standalone components only** — no NgModules
2. **Zoneless change detection** — never add `zone.js` imports or zone-dependent patterns
3. **Signals for state** — prefer `signal()`/`computed()`/`effect()` over manual subscriptions where possible
4. **OnPush everywhere** — `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`
5. **Angular Material** — use AM components consistently; don't roll custom UI that AM already covers
   - Exception (pacetrainer): the countdown ring (`pace-countdown-circle`) is a custom SVG, since `mat-progress-spinner` has no track ring
   - Exception (bacteria game): the stage's busy indicator (`feat-lazy-bac-game-bacteria-spinner`) is plain HTML and CSS, since it must keep moving on the compositor while the work it covers blocks the main thread
6. **Modern control flow** — `@if`, `@for`, `@switch` (not `*ngIf`, `*ngFor`, `*ngSwitch`)
7. **2-space indentation**, kebab-case filenames, `*.spec.ts` for tests
8. **Explicit `public`/`private`** in class members
9. **Strongly typed** — avoid `any`; use proper generics
10. **English in code** — identifiers, file and folder names, persisted field and storage key names, comments, commit messages, specs, plans and ADRs are English; texts the user sees stay in the app's UI language (German in Korbjäger and Pacetrainer). A domain term from `CONTEXT.md` takes its `_Code_` name (Kind is `Child`, Spiel `Game`, Kader `Roster`), never an ad-hoc translation. Fields of an outside API keep its spelling (the DBB's `ligaData`, `spielplan`) and get English names at the adapter. Korbjäger's existing German identifiers and Firestore fields are renamed by their own issues ([#2966](https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/issues/2966) the fields, then [#2967](https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/issues/2967) the identifiers), not piecemeal: persisted names need a migration. Pacetrainer's identifiers are English since [#2968](https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/issues/2968). Every non-persisted name a change introduces or rewrites is English
11. **Device storage through `@wolsok/utils-browser-storage`** — read, write and watch `localStorage` with `deviceStorage`, `readStored`/`writeStored`, `readStoredJson`/`writeStoredJson` and `watchStored` (`libs/utils/browser-storage`), never with a `try`/`catch` of your own: a missing, blocked or unreadable storage reads as nothing stored, a refused write keeps nothing and reports `'full'` or `'refused'`. Only `LocalAnswerCache` (`feat-korbjaeger-answers`), which evicts per failed write, keeps its own loop, and Korbjäger's `dropKeysBeforeEnglishNames` (`keys-before-english-names.ts`, transitional) keeps its guard until it goes

- One workspace-wide `.oxlintrc.json`; there are no per-project lint configs. Add project-specific rules through `overrides` with a `files` glob.
- Type-aware linting is on (`options.typeAware`, backed by `oxlint-tsgolint`). It reads each project's `tsconfig.json` with TypeScript 7 semantics: no `baseUrl`, `paths` relative to `tsconfig.base.json` (`./libs/...`), and no `moduleResolution: node`/`node10`. Keep new tsconfigs on that layout or lint reports `tsconfig-error`.
- `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries` runs inside oxlint through the `@nx/oxlint/boundaries-plugin` bridge; tag constraints live in `.oxlintrc.json`.
- Boundaries are never disabled inline: `wolsok/no-boundary-disable` (`tools/oxlint/workspace-rules.mjs`, the workspace's own JS plugin, a leaf project `oxlint-workspace-rules`: `@nx/oxlint` gives every project an implicit edge on a local plugin's project, so it must import nothing from the workspace) fails on `eslint-disable`/`oxlint-disable` comments for the rule. Move the import behind a lib's path alias, or record the exception as an override in `.oxlintrc.json` (as for `apps/*/federation.config.js` and `libs/utils/version`). That project's `namedInputs` `default` and `production` are empty, so the edge feeds no other project's `build`, `deploy` or `test` and a rule change releases nothing (#3015), while every `lint` still reads the plugin file; a target added to it names its inputs explicitly, as its `lint` and `test` do (`release-affected.test.mjs` checks every one).
- The workspace version (`version.json`) is read only through `@wolsok/utils-version` (`libs/utils/version`, `WORKSPACE_VERSION`, `releaseName(project)`), which declares the file as an input, so every task depending on it reruns on a release. `wolsok/no-version-json-read` (in the same `tools/oxlint/workspace-rules.mjs`) fails any other import or `read…()` of the file within one expression (`readFileSync(join(root, 'version.json'))`), but traces no path built in an earlier statement; `libs/utils/version` is exempt by an override in `.oxlintrc.json`. - Production sources never import test-only code: `wolsok/no-testing-import` (same plugin, on for `apps/*/src/**` and `libs/**/src/**` by an override in `.oxlintrc.json`) fails an import, `export … from`, `import()`, `import('…').Type`, `import x = require('…')` or `require()` of a `@wolsok/<lib>/testing` entry or a relative `testing` path, since those fakes call `jest.fn`/`vi.fn` at module load and the boundary rule counts `<lib>/testing` as `<lib>`.
